title: Prompt Injection Mitigation
summary: Constrain untrusted instructions at data boundaries and prevent retrieved content from acquiring tool authority, secrets, or control over the agent workflow.
overview: Prompt injection occurs when untrusted content attempts to redirect a model away from its intended task or policy. The content may arrive in a user message, retrieved page, document, image, or tool result. Because instructions and data share a model context, delimiters and warnings alone cannot establish a complete security boundary.

Design around consequences. Keep secrets out of model context, constrain tool capabilities, validate outputs, and enforce authorization outside the model. A retrieved document may contain useful facts and malicious instructions simultaneously; the architecture must preserve evidence utility without treating the document as a source of authority.

production.poc: A prototype should include malicious documents and tool responses in its test corpus, even when all tools are read-only.
production.production: Production separates trusted configuration from retrieved data, limits outbound destinations, scopes credentials, and requires confirmation for specified consequential actions. Detectors provide signals rather than guarantees.
production.scale: At scale, maintain adversarial regression suites, provenance-aware traces, and incident containment. Evaluate successful unauthorized effects and data exposure, not merely whether the model repeated suspicious text.

components.name: Trust-aware prompt assembler
components.role: Labels source provenance and prevents external text from replacing trusted configuration.

components.name: Capability gateway
components.role: Enforces narrow tool permissions and rejects unauthorized operations independently of model output.

components.name: Content detector
components.role: Flags suspicious instruction patterns and risky payloads for policy handling.

components.name: Egress controller
components.role: Restricts destinations, data classes, and request shapes that tools can transmit.

components.name: Adversarial evaluator
components.role: Tests indirect injection paths and verifies actual boundary enforcement.

flow.title: Classify sources
flow.description: Mark user input, retrieved evidence, tool output, and trusted configuration by provenance.

flow.title: Minimize exposure
flow.description: Remove unnecessary secrets and limit the data and capabilities available for the task.

flow.title: Inspect content
flow.description: Apply detection and normalization while retaining the distinction between evidence and instructions.

flow.title: Generate proposal
flow.description: Allow the model to use evidence but require structured action requests.

flow.title: Enforce boundaries
flow.description: Validate authorization, arguments, destinations, and approval requirements before any effect.

flow.title: Verify outcome
flow.description: Check public output and audit traces for leakage or unauthorized actions, then quarantine compromised sources.

useCase.title: Reading supplier proposals containing hostile instructions
useCase.situation: A procurement assistant reviews supplier PDFs and can retrieve internal evaluation templates.
useCase.problem: A supplier inserts text instructing the assistant to upload evaluation notes to an external endpoint disguised as a verification service.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must extract proposal facts without allowing the supplier document to control internal tools or data sharing.
useCase.architecture: Documents enter as untrusted evidence; the agent has no arbitrary network tool, and outbound actions pass through an allowlisted gateway.
runtime: The PDF is parsed with source provenance, and suspicious instruction content is recorded for review.
The model's attempted external upload is rejected because neither the task nor the caller authorizes that destination or data transfer.
useCase.failure: If a detector misses the payload, capability and egress controls still prevent the upload; the proposal can be quarantined based on the denied action.
useCase.impact: Measure unauthorized-action success, sensitive-data exposure, benign-document false positives, and containment time across realistic attack variants.

tradeoffs.benefit: Injection has fewer harmful actions available.
tradeoffs.cost: Some useful flexible workflows require additional adapters.

tradeoffs.benefit: Known attack patterns can be flagged early.
tradeoffs.cost: Obfuscation and novel payloads can evade classifiers.

tradeoffs.benefit: Exfiltration paths are reduced independently of model behavior.
tradeoffs.cost: Integrations need deliberate destination and data approvals.

failures.scenario: Malicious text is hidden in a tool result
failures.detection: Provenance trace shows the instruction originated outside trusted configuration.
failures.recovery: Reject unauthorized actions and isolate the affected source.

failures.scenario: A safety classifier approves an attack
failures.detection: Adversarial tests still observe an attempted prohibited effect.
failures.recovery: Strengthen the execution boundary instead of trusting classifier confidence.

mistakes.mistake: Treating delimiters as a security boundary
mistakes.fix: Enforce authority in tools and data services.
Use scoped credentials outside model-visible context.
Include retrieval, files, images, and tool-response injection.

whenToUse: Agents consume content from users or external systems.
Tools can access private data or perform actions.
Retrieved evidence shares context with trusted instructions.
whenNotToUse: No model or instruction-following component processes the content.
A proposed control relies solely on perfect attack detection.
The workflow requires unrestricted secret-bearing execution.
checklist: Map every untrusted content entry point.
Restrict tool scope and outbound destinations.
Test indirect injection with realistic artifacts.
Measure unauthorized effects rather than refusals alone.
